title: Energy-Flow Cosmology and Regime-Dependent Structure Formation (Paper III)
description: Paper III introduces Energy-Flow Cosmology (EFC), a thermodynamic framework in which entropy-gradient-driven energy flow governs regime-dependent structure formation across scales. Using a phenomenological decomposition E_total = E_flow + E_latent, the paper provides a unified interpretation consistent with the three-regime behavior seen in SPARC rotation curves (Paper I) and the early-time galaxy abundance excesses in JWST COSMOS-Web (Paper II), and it outlines testable predictions without replacing ΛCDM.

energy_flow_potential.description: Operational proxy for local energy available for organized flow, where \rho is local mass/energy density and S \in [0,1] is normalized entropy; higher density and lower entropy increase E_f.

energy_decomposition.description: Phenomenological split of total energy into a smoothly flowing component driven by entropy gradients and a latent component stored in non-equilibrium structures (e.g., bars, arms, tidal features).

latent_fraction.description: Latent energy fraction that determines regime membership: FLOW (L < 0.25), TRANSITION (0.25 \le L \le 0.45), LATENT (L > 0.45), with boundaries empirically motivated from SPARC.

key_results.main_finding: A single entropy-gradient-driven framework (EFC) consistently organizes both the three-regime behavior in galactic rotation curves and the accelerated early-universe structure formation seen by JWST.

sealed_predictions.statement: The three-regime classification based on latent fraction L (with empirically calibrated boundaries near 0.25 and 0.45) will reproducibly emerge in independent galaxy samples (e.g., LITTLE THINGS, DMS) and correlate with morphology/non-equilibrium features.
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: Re-analysis of independent rotation-curve datasets showing no statistically significant regime separation (e.g., Mann–Whitney or similar tests not rejecting the null at p < 0.01) or no correlation between L and morphological indicators (bar strength, tidal asymmetry).

sealed_predictions.statement: The galaxy abundance excess over ΛCDM will continue to increase monotonically with redshift beyond z > 10, persisting to z > 15 under conservative systematics.
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: Deep wide-field JWST/NGRST surveys showing no monotonic increase, or consistency with ΛCDM within 3σ across 8 < z < 15 after rigorous completeness and contamination corrections.

kill_criteria: KC1: Independent galaxy samples (e.g., LITTLE THINGS, DMS) fail to exhibit a statistically significant three-regime separation tied to L after calibration (e.g., p ≥ 0.01 across multiple tests).
KC2: Barred/high-asymmetry systems (high latent energy) show high rates of simple rotation-curve model success comparable to LSB systems across controlled samples.
KC3: Robust high-z surveys (z > 8) find no monotonic increase in abundance excess with redshift, or show compatibility with ΛCDM within 3σ from z ≈ 8 to z > 15 after stringent systematics treatment.
KC4: Quantitative proxies for entropy gradients (e.g., gas entropy, turbulence measures) do not correlate with predicted dynamical simplicity/complexity from E_f across diverse environments.
KC5: Systems classified as LATENT relax to core-like profiles on short timescales without corresponding decreases in latent energy content or non-equilibrium structure strength.
KC6: The empirically motivated regime boundaries for L fail to transfer (after reasonable recalibration) to multiple independent datasets, yielding inconsistent or non-reproducible classifications.
